comparison: Coordinate constraints must be combined before solving; the new circle task recovers its centre from a chord and centre line, then checks the origin is external before calculating tangent length.
Chained geometric constraints recover a locus; the new chord task reconstructs endpoints and two unknown ellipse axes.
An integration boundary changes when two expressions exchange order; the new absolute-value area also has a touching point and symmetry.
Trigonometric integration is calibrated as an accessible item; the new squared-sine substitution differs from the reference's sign-sensitive sine absolute value.
Composite-function differentiation is required; the new item derives inverse curvature through two chain-rule operations rather than only monotonicity.
Domain and map properties are distinguished; the new rational map is reconstructed and checked separately for inverse and fixed points.
Matrix algebra needs structural deductions; the new task constructs a cyclic polynomial, factors its determinant and excludes singular parameters before solving a trace condition.
A conditioned finite experiment changes the denominator; the new range-constrained ticket sample uses grouped subsets rather than the reference's altered urn.
Trigonometric sign and domain checks are relevant; this deliberately easier item solves a double-angle equation rather than claiming the reference's hard global-function demand.
Spatial normal or direction constraints precede angle/distance work; the new plane pencil includes a coefficient-zero endpoint before a point-plane distance.
Vector relations are translated into scalar constraints; the new pair of projection equations determines a norm ratio and dot product.
Unit-circle and angular information determine complex powers; the new distance-product transformation preserves conjugate branches.
Quadratic coefficients constrain roots; the new item deliberately exceeds the short reference by adding positivity, reciprocal separation and a finite integer domain.
Signed finite-binomial contributions require cancellation checks; the new product has two admissible exponent-pair routes, not a divisibility rewrite.
A GP is reconstructed before a requested sum; the new odd-index partition and squared-term sum use a different constraint structure.
Ellipse data feed a further geometric deduction; the new task uses two focal distances to recover a triangle height rather than a tangent-normal construction.
Absolute-value smoothness depends on the inner zero; the new item checks two derivatives at a flat trigonometric zero rather than counting piecewise-linear corners.
Expression changes require a split integral; the new parameter moves its breakpoint and must be checked both inside and outside the integration interval.
Map/relation properties need precise definitions; the new accessible finite-map task counts right inverses rather than testing a matrix relation.
Determinants and parameter branches are checked; the new entrywise adjugate identity imposes both off-diagonal and diagonal constraints.
Independent-event masses are combined before reporting a probability; the new accessible item then conditions on exactly one of two unequal-probability events.
A restricted counting construction is required; the new gap representation enforces no adjacent up steps before checking a forbidden vertex.
A finite binomial identity is evaluated; the new reciprocal weight requires integrating a finite expansion before identifying n and its central coefficient.
A self-referential partial-sum condition must be differenced; the new affine recurrence is shifted into a GP and its formula verified in the original identity.
Continuity constrains otherwise unknown behaviour; the new scaling identity uses finite halving and a limit before establishing differentiability.
An ODE is simplified by recognising a transformed dependent quantity; the new accessible homogeneous substitution finds a domain-checked first zero.
Spatial direction information feeds a metric construction; the new line half-turn requires projection, midpoint reconstruction and a coordinate sum.
Cross-product equalities constrain a vector direction; the new equality forces coplanarity and includes zero and equal-vector degeneracies.
Dispersion definitions must be respected; the new item is substantially more demanding than the reference shift by requiring two mean-location cases and integer-frequency rejection.
Trigonometric sign information controls an identity; the new symmetric tangent constraints recover a cosine difference without solving individual angles.
